claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy contains well-defined dual nanoprecipitates dispersed in a solid-solution matrix.
In situ characterization during high-temperature oxidation can elucidate time-dependent oxide formation and oxidation mechanisms.
ETEM can provide near-atomic-resolution imaging during oxidation.
High-resolution EDS mapping in ETEM can resolve elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces during oxidation.
High-temperature oxidation induces atomic-scale elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces in additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Al and Cr migrate between nanoprecipitates and the matrix across nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces during oxidation.
Oxide formation can redistribute an oxide-forming element and deplete that element from the bulk alloy.
Elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces governs whether protective or nonprotective oxide phases form.
Sufficient formation of Al2O3 or Cr2O3 produces a protective oxide scale in this alloy.
Nonprotective oxides can form during high-temperature oxidation of high-entropy alloys.
Interfacial elemental redistribution influences overall oxidation kinetics and degradation behavior.
Sequential ETEM/EDS observations will show a measurable correlation between elemental redistribution and the onset and identity of oxide scales.
Protective oxide scales are associated with enhanced oxidation resistance.
Formation of nonprotective oxides indicates an oxidation-degradation mechanism.
Previous ex situ analyses did not resolve near-atomic-scale elemental redistribution dynamics during oxidation.
Maintaining an oxidizing environment and sufficient temporal resolution in ETEM may impede precise quantification of elemental migration.
The proposed conclusions are limited to Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 under the tested oxidation conditions.
Failure to observe significant interfacial redistribution, or observation that oxide-scale identity is independent of redistribution, would falsify the hypothesis.
